style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; em-dashes used sparingly

1.text: Oh, the blessedness, the deep and settled happiness of the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, taking their advice as the rule for his life; who does not stand in the way that sinners take; who does not, at the last, sink down into the seat of the mockers.
1.amp: Oh, the blessedness! The deep and settled happiness [ashre -- a heaped-up Hebrew exclamation, 'the blessednesses of...'] of the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked [refusing their advice as his guide], nor stand in the way of sinners [refusing their pattern of life], nor settle into the seat of mockers [the scoffer's chair, where contempt for God hardens into a habit].
1.notes: 'ashre (H835), plural construct: 'O the blessednesses of...' The threefold walk -> stand -> sit (H1980/H5975/H3427) traces deepening entanglement; letsim (H3887) = scoffers/mockers.

2.text: Instead, his whole delight is set on the instruction of the LORD, and over that instruction he broods, chewing it and murmuring it low to himself, day and night.
2.amp: Instead, his delight is in the instruction [torah -- the law, teaching, and direction] of the LORD, and on that instruction he meditates [hagah -- he mutters and growls it low, chewing it over the way an animal works its food] day and night.
2.notes: torah (H8451) = instruction/teaching, broader than 'law'; hagah (H1897) = to mutter/growl/murmur -- chewing the words over aloud, not silent reflection.

3.text: He stands like a tree transplanted beside flowing streams, deliberately set where the water never fails, yielding its fruit when its season comes; its leaves stay green and never wither, and whatever such a man sets his hand to ripens and comes through to good.
3.amp: He stands like a tree transplanted [shathal -- deliberately set, not self-sprung] beside flowing streams [peleg -- drawn irrigation channels that never run dry], yielding its fruit when its season comes; its leaf never withering, and whatever he does ripens and prospers [tsalach -- pushes through to success].
3.notes: shathal (H8362) = transplanted/deliberately set; peleg (H6388) = drawn irrigation channels (steady water), not a wild river; tsalach (H6743) = to push forward, succeed.

4.text: Not so the wicked, not so at all! They are mere chaff, the dry and weightless husk that the threshing wind lifts and scatters, with nothing to hold it down.
4.amp: Not so the wicked [they have no such rootedness]! They are mere chaff [mots -- the worthless husk threshed off the grain], which the wind drives off and scatters [weightless, with nothing to anchor them].
4.notes: mots (H4671) = chaff, the husk blown off in threshing -- rootless and weightless, the deliberate opposite of the planted tree. The doubled 'not so' reflects the Hebrew emphasis.

5.text: And so the wicked will not stand, unable to rise and hold their ground when the judgment comes; nor will sinners take their place in the assembly of the righteous.
5.amp: Therefore the wicked will not stand [qum -- rise to their feet and hold their ground] when the judgment comes, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous [edah -- God's gathered, covenant people].
5.notes: qum (H6965) = to rise/stand firm -- the wicked cannot hold their ground under judgment; edah (H5712) = the congregation/assembly of God's people.

6.text: For the LORD intimately knows the way of the righteous; He marks it, guards it, and owns it as His own. But the way of the wicked leads nowhere, and in the end it perishes.
6.amp: For the LORD knows [yada -- not mere awareness but watchful, claiming care] the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish [abad -- vanish, be lost, come to nothing].
6.notes: yada (H3045) = to know intimately/relationally -- to acknowledge, watch over, and own; abad (H6) = to perish/vanish/be lost.
